assertions: The ship is not sunk or wrecked — she is living and still afloat, her bulk/hull essentially intact despite the repeated reports of wreck
The peril was real but not fatal: Saturn in Aries in the 11th squaring the Ascendant very nearly shows danger, damage-scare and loss of hope/friends' help, not total loss of the ship
The ship and those aboard are safe: the Moon, lady of the Ascendant, is in Taurus in the 11th in her exaltation and near the body of Jupiter, a strong protection that outweighs Saturn's square
She is to the southward, close to land on the coast she was sent to trade to — the Spanish coast — lying near shore/harbour in earth-sign (Taurus/Capricorn) quarters, not lost in the open sea
News of her will come very soon, within a few days rather than weeks or months: the Moon applies by trine to Mercury, significator of tidings, in the 7th, wanting but a few minutes of a perfect trine
The coming news will be good and will contradict the wreck reports and the insurers: the trine is to the Sun and Mercury in the 7th, from the foreign/opposite quarter of her trading voyage
method: Horary astrology (Lilly, Christian Astrology Book II), classical horary judgment from the chart positions given in the question
reasoning: Ascendant Cancer signifies the bulk/body of the ship. Saturn in Aries in the 11th in near square to the Ascendant explains the wreck rumours, danger and refusal of insurers, but does not destroy the significator. The Moon, lady of the Ascendant, is exalted in Taurus in the 11th and close to Jupiter, showing the ship preserved and living. Her immediate application by trine (only minutes from perfect) to the Sun and Mercury in the 7th brings imminent, favourable tidings via Mercury as news-bearer, from the 7th/foreign quarter. Earth signs Taurus and Capricorn and the 9th-house voyage context place her southward close to the land/coast of her Spanish trading destination; South Node in the 9th accounts for affliction and false loss reports on the voyage without total loss. Timing scale is days because the question asks for imminent news of a current voyage and the applying aspect is minutes from perfection.
summary: The ship is not sunk but living and safe near the Spanish coast, and good news of her will arrive within a few days.
